scope: only the eight concepts restored in the drafter's Round 2 section (2, 4, 12, 13, 17, 18, 20, 22); the rest passed two rounds

concepts.why: Every passage sets 'former' (or, in 2 Cor 5:17, 'old') against 'new', and the name is a plain label that asserts no more. Notes are exact quotations. It does not say any Old Testament verse is fulfilled in a New Testament one.

Name is Gen 3:17 plus Rev 22:3 in their own words; Gen 8:21 ('Never again will I curse the ground') sits between them as the text's own statement about the ground's curse. The concept does not say Rev 22:3 undoes Gen 3:17. Notes exact.

concepts.name: Tears, weeping, and sorrow
concepts.why: Biblical-theological / academic reader: the name 'He will wipe away every tear' is said only by Isa 25:8, Rev 7:17 and Rev 21:4. Isa 35:10 says 'sorrow and sighing will flee' and Isa 65:19 says 'weeping and crying will no longer be heard', and neither mentions tears or wiping. A plain label that covers all five passages is accurate (tears: Isa 25:8, Rev 7:17, 21:4; weeping: Isa 65:19, Rev 21:4; sorrow: Isa 35:10). Alternative if the drafter prefers to keep the Rev 21:4 phrase as the name: drop Isa 35:10 and Isa 65:19. All notes are exact quotations.

Each passage says 'new covenant' in its own words (Jer 31:34 is the content of the same oracle as 31:31). The name 'A new covenant' states the shared phrase only and claims neither identity nor fulfilment between Jeremiah and the New Testament verses; Heb 8:8 quotes Jer 31:31 outright. Notes exact.

concepts.name: Light, and no more night
concepts.why: Secular/academic and biblical-theological reader: 'There will be no more night' is Rev 22:5 and 21:25. Isa 60:19 says the sun and moon will no longer be the light and the LORD will be the light, Isa 60:20 says the sun will no longer set, Rev 21:23 says no need of sun or moon, and Zech 14:7 says 'without day or night; but when evening comes, there will be light'. None of those four says 'no night', and Zech 14:7 even says 'without day'. A plain label naming what all six share (light, and night gone or the sun and moon unneeded) stays within the texts. Notes are exact quotations.

Plain label; every passage has water flowing out (Ezek 47:1, 9, 12; Joel 3:18; Zech 14:8; Rev 22:1). Each note uses that passage's own words. Silent on whether Ezekiel's temple is literal or figurative, and on timing, so the dispensational, amillennial and Jewish readers can all accept it.

Name is Rev 22:17. Isa 55:1, John 7:37 and Rev 22:17 invite the thirsty to come; John 4:14 and Rev 21:6 say the thirsty receive water. All five hold the thirsty being given water. Notes exact. Minor: John 4:14 and Rev 21:6 do not say 'come', but the concept is not weakened by them.

Name is Isa 65:21; Ezek 28:26 and Amos 9:14 say building or rebuilding, dwelling, and planting vineyards in their own words, and Isa 65:22 develops the same verse. The concept makes no claim about when these happen or whether they are one time or several, which is the point where the readers of the last things divide. Notes exact.
